data.text:
JUST IN: The Manila city government clarified it has no objections to the demonstrations for Baha sa Luneta 2.0 on Sunday, Nov. 30, but stresses the need for its organizers to have proper coordination with concerned agencies amid reports of people being prevented by the police to conduct their rally in the area due to lack of permit.

"LGU Manila interposes no objection to the protest rally. We will provide the same assistance (traffic, garbage and emergency medical assistance) as we did during the Sept. 21 rally and the Nov. 16-18 peace rally. However, Roxas Blvd is under the jurisdiction of the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA), and Luneta is under the National Parks Development Committee (NPDC). They should coordinate directly with them. That was our advice to the rally organizers in a meeting held in the city hall last Nov. 25, 2025," Mayor Francisco "Isko Moreno" Domagoso said.

"No rally permit is needed from any local or national agency for Liwasang Bonifacio, as it is a Freedom Park," he added. | via Patrick Garcia

Labor groups arrive at the People Power Monument in Quezon City for the “Trillion Peso March” on Bonifacio Day, November 30, 2025. 

The protest highlights workers’ demands for higher wages, job security, and accountability over the alleged misuse of public funds amounting to trillions of pesos. 

Demonstrators also denounce corruption, rising prices of basic goods, and the continued burden of taxes on ordinary Filipinos, calling for transparent governance and genuine economic reforms. | via Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News
